title: Primary Care Provider Assignment Access Standards for Assigned Practices
content:
The practice that holds a member's **Primary Care Provider Assignment** must meet the access standards of its practice type.

## Standard

The assigned practice offers routine appointments within the practice type's routine appointment days and urgent appointments within its urgent appointment hours, a same-day sick visit where the practice type requires one, an after-hours clinician callback within its callback minutes, and an interpreter at no cost for the listed languages. A member who reports that the practice failed an access standard may change PCP for access problem.

## Access schedule

| Practice type | Routine appointment within (days) | Urgent appointment within (hours) | Same-day sick visit required | Around-the-clock clinician line required | After-hours callback within (minutes) |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Standard Primary Care Provider | 21 | 48 | No | Yes | 30 |
| Pediatric Primary Care Provider | 14 | 24 | Yes | Yes | 30 |
| OB/GYN Primary Care Provider | 14 | 48 | No | Yes | 30 |
| Federally Qualified Health Center Home | 21 | 48 | No | Yes | 30 |
| Patient-Centered Medical Home Practice | 14 | 24 | Yes | Yes | 20 |
| Specialist Serving as PCP | 30 | 48 | No | Yes | 30 |
| Health Home Lead Provider | 14 | 24 | Yes | Yes | 20 |

**Interpreter languages.** For every practice type the practice arranges a qualified interpreter at no cost for Spanish, Vietnamese, Somali, Arabic and other languages.

## Applying the standard (hypothetical reports)

- A member of a Pediatric Primary Care Provider is offered a first routine appointment 20 days out. The standard is 14 days, so the practice failed it and the member may change PCP for access problem.
- A member of a Standard Primary Care Provider is offered a routine appointment 20 days out. That is within 21 days.
- A member of a Health Home Lead Provider calls after hours and is called back by a clinician after 25 minutes. The standard is 20 minutes, so the practice failed it.
- A member of an OB/GYN Primary Care Provider asks for a same-day sick visit. The practice type does not require one.
